name: Operations Picture: one map, three layers, act where you stand
thesis: Every ERIS object is a place on the state highway system: a field report, the Event Group it belongs to, the Assessment it spawned and the technical form the engineer writes are all pins at the same Route/Post-Mile. Today the web splits them across seven pages (My Work, Mission Center, Incidents, Event Groups, Assessments, Submissions, Photo evidence) that each show a different slice with a different vocabulary and only two of those pages ever put map and list on screen together (and only at 1440px). The redesign collapses them into one viewport-locked surface, the Map, with three switchable layers (Incidents, Event Groups, Assessments) and one synchronized list. 'Waiting on me' is a filter chip with a count, not a page: turn it on and the map and list show only the pins whose next step belongs to the signed-in person, grouped by what they must do. Selecting a pin or a row opens the same detail panel everywhere (right panel on desktop, drill-in panel on iPad landscape, draggable bottom sheet on phone and iPad portrait) and the workflow action for that step is performed inside the panel through a labelled action sheet, so record-browsing and acting are never two places. Long work leaves the map deliberately: the technical form, terrain tool, intake report and admin consoles are full-screen routes that open pre-centred on the selected site and return to the map at the same pin. A newcomer learns three things in the first minute (the map, the layer chips, the Waiting-on-me count) and everything else is one tap from a pin. Baseline to beat and how: phone content starts at 700px today, on the Map it starts at 56px with the list peeking in the first viewport; My Work is 2.9 screens tall today, the Map is exactly 1.0 with a single scrolling region; the technical form is 11.1 screens with a 532px canvas in a 375px viewport, the new task-list hub is 1.4 screens with zero horizontal overflow; 120 sub-40px tap targets and 74 sub-12px text nodes on that page become 0 by rule.

principles.name: Place before ID
principles.statement: Every row, pin, panel header and notification leads with the site (District 7 · Los Angeles · Route 101 · PM 12.30 and the incident title), then the plain status, then who holds it and for how long. Numeric ids (Incident #40, Assessment #12, Form #9) appear once, muted, at the end of the header for cross-reference and never as the first word.

principles.name: One surface, one selection, one scroll
principles.statement: The Map is viewport-locked at every width. Exactly one region scrolls at a time (the list, the sheet, or the panel), never a page that contains a map that contains a list. Selection is a single URL state (?layer=&id=) so map pin, list row and panel always agree, deep links open the right panel, and Back closes the panel instead of losing the filter.

principles.name: Act where you stand, confirm only what cannot be undone
principles.statement: Each detail panel has one 'What happens next' card with the single primary action for the viewer's role at this step. Routine hand-offs (review report, delegate, assign, add reviewer, submit) run in a labelled action sheet with a consequence sentence above the button and no separate confirm; irreversible or notifying actions (approve, return for changes, finalize, close incident, disable account, publish dataset) require the sheet's confirm step with the note field inside it. Every action ends with a toast that names the object and where it went, and the row moves to 'Recently handled by me' instead of vanishing.

principles.name: Show what the decision needs, hide what the database needs
principles.statement: Each panel and page lists its essential fields explicitly (below) and everything else is behind a 'Details' disclosure or absent. Internal codes (COORDINATOR_REVIEW, NORTH, FIELD_WORKER, SRID, job UUIDs, six-decimal coordinates) never render as primary text; they are replaced by names, plain status phrases and a copy-coordinates button.

principles.name: Composition per width, not shrinking
principles.statement: Four window-size classes (compact <600, medium 600-839, expanded 840-1199, large >=1200) each get a designed composition: bottom bar + sheet, rail + sheet, rail + drill-in panel, rail + list + map + panel. Panels are written once with container queries so the same incident panel works at 360px in a sheet, 440px docked, and full width on a phone page. Touch targets are 44px on coarse pointers and 24px minimum anywhere, and every map interaction has a list equivalent.

principles.name: Teach in place, never in a tour
principles.statement: No welcome carousel. Learning happens through a Help control in the same header slot on every page (WCAG 3.2.6) that opens 'How your part of the workflow works' in 4 steps for the signed-in role, a glossary, and support contact; through teaching empty states that say why the list is empty and what will appear; through plain status labels with a next-step sentence; and through the consequence sentence on every action sheet.

navigation.model: A single hub route /map with layer, filter and selection in the URL (/map?layer=incidents&mine=1&id=40, plus /map?view=list for the table form). Up to four top-level destinations per role plus an account menu: Map (the hub, carrying the Waiting-on-me count badge), Report (new incident intake, only for roles that can file), Tools (Terrain cross sections), Admin (Users, Road inventory) and Account (avatar menu: name, humanized roles, appearance, help, sign out). Records pages, My Work and Mission Center are not destinations: /my-work redirects to /map?mine=1, /incidents to /map?layer=incidents, /incidents/:id to /map?layer=incidents&id=:id, /event-groups(/:id) and /assessments(/:id) likewise, /mission-center/:gid/:iid to /map?layer=incidents&id=:iid&tab=evidence. Full-screen work routes (/incidents/new, /submissions/:id, /gis/terrain-cross-sections, /admin/*) render inside the same shell with a 'Back to map' control that restores the previous map state from history.
navigation.desktop: Large (>=1200): a persistent 72px vertical navigation rail on the left (icon + 11-12px label stacked, 56px-tall items, brand fill on the active item, count badge on Map) implemented with the existing useNavSections and NavItem; no collapse toggle and no hamburger. The header is a 56px bar: ERIS mark linking to /map, the current place (page title or breadcrumb), a Help icon button, and the avatar menu. On the Map the header also hosts the search field. Rail + header replace the 256px sidebar, the stacked 'Navigation' card, the raw-role identity line, the theme select and the footer.
navigation.tablet: Expanded (840-1199, iPad landscape): the same 72px rail, same header. Medium (600-839, iPad portrait or half-width Split View): same 72px rail (it costs 7% of width and keeps the mental model identical); the list and detail become a bottom sheet as on phone but with two-column rows. In workspace routes (technical form, terrain tool) the rail stays visible; nothing is hidden behind a hamburger at any tablet width.
navigation.phone: Compact (<600): a 56px bottom navigation bar with 3-4 items (Map, Report when allowed, Tools/Admin when allowed, Account) plus safe-area padding, and a 56px top header (ERIS mark, place title, Help, avatar). No drawer, no hamburger. The Map fills the space between header and bar; the list and detail live in a draggable bottom sheet with three detents (peek 96px, half 50%, full). Full-screen work routes hide the bottom bar and show a sticky 'Back' in the header plus a sticky bottom action bar for their primary action.

/map?layer=incidents&mine=1 where 'mine' means items explicitly assigned to this account, not every queue in the state; an 'All queues' toggle inside the filter reveals the statewide firehose on demand

navigation.rationale: Baymard measured that 65% of users never engage a map hidden behind a tab while 95% engage a persistent split view; Esri's dashboard guidance and Calcite both model list-map sync and start-side panels; NN/g's hamburger study shows hidden navigation costs 20% discoverability and 39% slower desktop tasks, so the rail is always visible above 600px. Capping destinations at four per role follows Apple HIG and the research brief ('never more than five'), while Material's adaptive-navigation rule gives the bottom bar / rail split at 600px. Making 'Waiting on me' a filter rather than a page removes the My Work vs Assessments confusion that every first-day walkthrough hit (identical layouts, one 'act', one 'browse') and guarantees the actionable item is always found where the record is found. Redirecting every legacy route keeps bookmarks, mobile deep links and email links working during migration.

touchAndDensityRules: Every interactive element is at least 24x24 CSS px with 8px spacing anywhere (WCAG 2.5.8) and at least 44x44 px under @media (pointer: coarse) via a shared utility class applied to buttons, chips, row actions, sort headers, checkboxes, sheet handle, map controls and thumbnails.
Row height 48px on coarse pointers and 40px on fine pointers; 32px compact only on fine pointers; preference stored per user.
No text below 12px; captions 12-13px, body 14px, phone form inputs 16px to prevent iOS zoom; the 74 tiny text nodes and 120 small targets on today's form page become 0.
Nothing essential lives in a hover-only tooltip or title attribute; hints are visible text or a tap-to-open info button.
Exactly one scroll region per screen state: the map is fixed, the sheet/panel scrolls; the SceneView and MapView are never inside a scrolling container.
Status is never colour-only: shape + text label for pins, light-background text tags for statuses, one fixed colour per status from the existing tokens (--brand, --good, --bad, --accent, --muted).
Every map interaction has a list equivalent; the list is keyboard-navigable with aria-current on the selected row; the panel is a landmark region with a heading.
Reflow: at 320px width nothing but the map itself and wide tables (behind their own overflow container) scrolls horizontally; filters, headers, forms and dialogs reflow.
Density of information is set per screen by the essential lists above; anything not listed is behind a Details disclosure or a tab, never a second card.
Dialogs and sheets have max-height calc(100dvh - 2rem) with internal scroll and sticky footers; backdrop tap does not dismiss while a form is dirty.

Statewide layers can grow to thousands of pins; mitigated by server-side bbox/scope filters (backend change 1), scale-dependent clustering and the default 'mine/my district/my office' scopes.

A nonmodal draggable bottom sheet is easy to get wrong for keyboard and screen-reader users; mitigated by detent changes via arrow keys, a visible 'Expand list' button as the equivalent control, inert map at full detent, and the table view as a fallback.

Until backend changes 3 and 5 land, the technical form still has two state machines and no web photo upload; the phase plan hides the form-level submit behind the assessment action and shows a clear 'Photos are added in the mobile app' notice so the walkthrough failures do not recur silently.
Users habituated to My Work and Mission Center URLs: redirects keep every old path working and the first-visit help names the change once.
Route normalisation (80 / I-80 / 080 / R080) needs a maintained alias table; start with numeric normalisation and county-route prefixes, extend from search logs.
Panel width of 440px is tight for the assessment pipeline plus quoted comments on 1200-1280px laptops; the list rail collapses to 56px automatically below 1366px when a panel is open.
Bulk actions for chiefs (assign many after a storm) are deferred; individual actions are 4-5 taps each, acceptable for typical volumes but should be measured.

Offline use on iPad web is not supported; the mobile app remains the offline tool and the web form shows an 'Offline - changes stored on this device' chip only for in-session autosave recovery, not for true offline work.
